batch_strategy: Use matched loading contrasts and solvent-response experiments around measured failures, with controlled checks of response shape and one chemically motivated new-graph transfer test. All choices use the same catalog and its supplied premeasurement predictions.

choices.reason: m205 at 2/1 and 100 uL, predicted 20.45/45.53 mL, supplies a loading comparison to measured 150-uL row 91b6bda771851a5c78ac. Together with the selected 100-uL 5/1 point, it tests whether loading modifies this primary alcohol's steep solvent response.

m205 at 5/1 and 100 uL, predicted 44.36/86.59 mL, lies between measured 50- and 150-uL rows 7954bf73f74c7fbcecb2 and e8f592c469b2f3c136d8. The intermediate loading can distinguish a reproducible endpoint response from variability in the two existing records.

m212 at 5/1 and 100 uL, predicted 14.27/28.59 mL, brackets measured 50-uL endpoints of 7.24/13.67 in d5234e966aa231be05e5 and 150-uL endpoints of 23.21/39.84 in 89d752b5a7f7c8d0b91e. Tests the opposite loading direction from several alcohol examples.

m212 at 10/1 and 100 uL, predicted 32.89/57.49 mL, extends the selected same-loading 5/1 point. Measured d5234e966aa231be05e5 and 89d752b5a7f7c8d0b91e show why solvent response must be separated from loading in this secondary amine.

m212 at 1/1 and 100 uL, predicted 7.42/13.03 mL, completes a same-loading 1/1–5/1–10/1 experiment. It tests whether the large measured 5/1 loading contrast is confined to a retained regime or reflects a broader scaffold-specific relationship.

m51 at 2/1 and 150 uL, predicted 9.82/16.12 mL, extends the low-ratio side of measured 150-uL 1/1 row 3c43e519a9cf66b66ebc. Its well-bracketed 10/1 loading response in 4fb92bd1fab3ba235858, bad24d96575f423fe4fd and 19229d505f75d05a0bcb provides a retained-regime reference.

m141 at 1/1 and 100 uL, predicted 8.73/21.11 mL, compares directly with measured 150-uL row de4e10d3a5d448ffcdda. This stronger-eluent loading contrast complements the substantial onset contrast measured at 10/1.

m141 at 10/1 and 150 uL, predicted 29.21/68.41 mL, completes a loading sequence with measured 50- and 100-uL rows 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0 and abca62b372239d49a61b. Tests whether onset continues decreasing while completion remains comparatively stable.

m118 at 10/1 and 150 uL, predicted 9.16/38.53 mL, compares with measured 100-uL row 319e89d7000731f64e7f at 4.78/36.82. Its broad V1 quantile spread and the retained 20/1 result fc27fa779102c4aeb8ab motivate separating onset behavior from completion transfer.

m118 at 5/1 and 150 uL, predicted 5.61/27.67 mL, pairs with selected 10/1 at identical loading. The measured 2/1 row ce1e18cf41501bc573ad and 20/1 row fc27fa779102c4aeb8ab bracket the broader response at different loadings.

m128 at 5/1 and 100 uL, predicted 11.54/27.01 mL, pairs with selected 100-uL 10/1. Measured 150-uL rows 34aaca6f7a0768d743fe and 596bd04bfe916866f908 establish a substantial 2/1-to-10/1 increase, making the intermediate ratio informative about sulfur/carbonyl-context transfer.

m128 at 10/1 and 100 uL, predicted 30.06/53.70 mL, directly tests loading transfer from measured 150-uL row 596bd04bfe916866f908 at 33.83/57.29. The current prediction has already adapted to that historical failure; this label tests the remaining local relationship.

m92 at 50/1 and 50 uL, predicted 27.73/59.74 mL, compares directly with measured 100-uL row 9862563d18aae2868342 at 27.45/51.70. Tests loading transfer after 4b8ba288d549f6cfc94b, 8b58e9d7a710f55e49d3 and 9862563d18aae2868342 established its nonflat solvent response.

m31 at 10/1 and 50 uL, predicted 35.21/75.70 mL, tests the large predicted increase beyond measured 5/1 row f0b6d8fb9d1feea8b24b at 100 uL. Measured 50-uL 1/1 row 386303f0b10c49ce93b4 provides a same-loading anchor for this carbonyl/nitrile graph.

hypotheses.content: m205 has a steep solvent response at 150-uL loading, with completion increasing from 10.85 through 34.09 and 50.98 to 100.95 mL at 0/1, 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1. Its loading dependence varies with ratio and endpoint.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate loading labels can constrain the interaction between solvent ratio and loading without extending m205's historical error as a uniform correction to related alcohols.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected 100-uL 2/1 and 5/1 results interpolate between existing loadings, or reveal additional nonlinearity?

hypotheses.content: Earlier onset at larger loading recurs in some retained scaffolds, but its transfer across molecules and solvent ratios is weakened by the opposite m212 5/1 and m205 1/1 contrasts. The predictor remains comparatively insensitive to loading.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched contrasts can teach scaffold- and ratio-dependent loading relationships separately for V1 and V2. The contradictory directions argue against a universal monotonic adjustment.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does intermediate m212 loading support its measured increasing-retention direction, and does m141 retain its onset-specific trend across three loadings?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl-containing molecules have distinct structure-by-ratio responses. Recent sulfur-substituted ketone retention, lower naphthaldehyde retention than its acquisition prediction, and heterogeneous ester and nitrile/carbonyl curves limit transfer based on carbonyl count or aromaticity alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate-ratio labels and direct loading comparisons can localize corrections to graph and conditions, reducing overcorrection of ordinary carbonyl and ester rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do m118, m128 and m31 enter their more retained regimes, and do their endpoint responses transfer across loading?

hypotheses.content: Recent beta-dicarbonyl labels reveal opposite acquisition errors across graph environments: m26 and m168 were overpredicted at weak eluent, whereas m94 at 10/1 was substantially underpredicted. A shared response based on carbonyl count is inadequate.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Comparisons across beta-ketoesters and substituted beta-diketones provide supervision for distinct onset and completion curves. Enol populations and intramolecular hydrogen bonding remain possible explanations, not measured mechanisms.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m94 continue its retained response at 20/1 while m166, m167 and m168 preserve earlier onset and more modest completion growth?

hypotheses.content: Valid m45 measurements increase substantially from 10/1 to 20/1 at 50 uL. The 50/1, 100-uL record has negative completion and reversed endpoints, leaving the physical response at that loading unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The matched 100-uL 20/1 label can distinguish loading dependence from propagation of an anomalous record into neighboring predictions without assuming that any existing label should be altered.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 100 uL, does 20/1 retention resemble the valid 50-uL result or remain near the much lower current prediction?

hypotheses.content: Substantial retention is measured across several ring-nitrogen, amino-ester and alcohol environments, but its onset threshold and completion growth differ by graph and loading. Late labels should constrain those boundaries rather than produce a broad heteroatom correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected local experiments test whether learned high-retention behavior transfers across loading and neighboring ratios in several recurring chemical families.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which families preserve their measured response across loading, and which develop an additional solvent-dependent shift?

hypotheses.content: For m99 at identical 50-uL loading, the model predicts completion falling from 27.90 mL at 1/1 to 16.54 mL at 2/1. This may be a localized response-shape artifact, although nonmonotonicity cannot be rejected from chemical prior alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The controlled pair can resolve a specific strong-eluent prediction shape without imposing monotonicity on all molecules or confusing loading changes with solvent response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does measured m99 completion actually decrease from 1/1 to 2/1 under matched loading conditions?

feedback_interpretation:
This correction uses the same measured records and supplied predictions, with no new label information. The latest m205 results establish a steep 150-uL solvent curve while weakening a universal loading interpretation: at 1/1, the larger loading eluted later, whereas at 5/1 its onset was slightly earlier and completion later. The m212 5/1 contrast also runs opposite to the recurring earlier-onset-at-higher-loading pattern. Conversely, the intermediate m51 result supports a graded onset response with comparatively stable completion, and m141 adds another onset-sensitive loading contrast.

The m26 and m168 weak-eluent results were substantially below their acquisition predictions, while m94 at 10/1 was above prediction. These outcomes sharpen the structural boundary within beta-dicarbonyl chemistry. m128 exposed further retention, whereas m195 at 50/1 was much earlier than its acquisition prediction; neither result supports a blanket carbonyl correction. The valid m45 10/1 and 20/1 pair rejects the predicted decline at 50-uL loading, but does not resolve the anomalous 100-uL 50/1 record.

The m4 measurements rejected its predicted intermediate-ratio maximum, and m191 completion at 1/1 was below measured 2/1. However, m117 genuinely decreased in completion from measured 1/1 to 2/1, so the new m99 shape test is posed as a controlled question rather than a monotonicity rule. Accurate recent m87 and m180 outcomes reduce the value of repeating dense local curves there. All historical error statements refer to acquisition-time predictions.
batch_rationale:
The batch emphasizes relationships that can generalize across recurring rows. Two m205 labels test intermediate loading at different solvent strengths. The m212 three-ratio experiment incorporates an intermediate loading bracket, while m141 receives matched stronger-eluent and retained-regime comparisons. m51 adds a stronger-eluent anchor after its three-loading 10/1 sequence supported an onset trend.

Carbonyl and ester selections combine response-curve gaps with loading comparisons around recent failures. The beta-dicarbonyl group discriminates graph environments with opposing historical errors. The matched m99 pair tests a particular predicted completion decrease. The m45 20/1 point constrains a region affected by invalid endpoint ordering using the loading of existing 10/1 and anomalous 50/1 records. One new m139 graph tests transfer of ordinary aromatic behavior against a specific measured iodotoluene reference.

The remaining experiments constrain retained nitrogen-containing and donor-containing families through meaningful neighboring conditions. These choices balance failure repair with ordinary-retention transfer and controlled response experiments. Selected IDs are distinct candidate-table records, and selected condition tuples are distinct. Their supplied premeasurement predictions are fixed with this selection. Quantile spreads and CW distances are auxiliary single-model evidence, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty; V2 minus V1 is an elution interval. Loading mass is the supplied density-times-volume feature. Differences in recorded loading conditions are retained as limitations, and unrecorded experimental factors may contribute to variability. Expected benefit is improved structure-by-condition supervision after retraining, rather than better chromatographic performance of the selected runs themselves.
